question: Why is surgical evacuation necessary alongside antibiotic therapy in septic abortion?

options.B: Antibiotics cannot enter the bloodstream of a pregnant woman
options.C: Infected retained tissue keeps the infection active
options.D: Curettage removes the need to monitor urine output

question: Which medication is commonly used to help empty the uterus during an inevitable abortion?

options.A: Ergometrine tablets
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Oxytocin nasal spray
options.D: Misoprostol

question: Why does a baby in an OP position often develop swelling (caput succedaneum) on the head?

options.A: Too much oxygen entering the fetal brain during contractions
options.B: An infection caught inside the amniotic fluid before labor begins
options.C: Prolonged pressure from the cervix against the tightly fitted pelvic bones
options.D: A genetic condition affecting how skin grows on the scalp

question: How does the honeycomb arrangement of spongy bone benefit the human body?

question: Why must sebaceous glands continuously produce new cells in their basal layer?

question: Which food item is commonly known to help reduce stool odor in ostomy patients?

options.A: Yogurt

options.D: Onions

question: What dangerous event defines a strangulated hernia?

options.A: Loss of blood supply to the trapped tissue

question: Why should a nurse use a draw sheet instead of pulling a patient directly across the bottom sheet?

options.A: To keep the bottom mattress completely dry

options.D: To warm up the patient's body quickly

question: A pregnant woman's blood test shows a very high level of alpha-fetoprotein. What condition should the midwife suspect first?

options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Severe iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Pregnancy-induced hypertension

question: Why must surface water sources like rivers always undergo rigorous treatment before being given to pregnant women?

options.A: They lack dissolved oxygen required for human cellular metabolism
options.B: They are too warm to safely quench the thirst of a laboring mother
options.C: They naturally contain dangerously high levels of essential table salt
options.D: They are constantly exposed to animal feces, human waste, and agricultural chemicals

explanation: Open water bodies collect runoff and waste from many sources, making them heavily laden with pathogens and toxins. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why do many young girls experience irregular menstrual cycles during the first year or two after menarche?

options.A: The ovaries have not yet developed any functional egg follicles
options.B: Immature feedback mechanisms within the HPG axis often lead to anovulatory cycles
options.C: Constant dietary changes in secondary schools disrupt uterine lining shedding
options.D: Severe physical exhaustion from household chores stops hormone production

question: What is a common metabolic problem to watch for in a newborn delivered by a mother with pre-gestational diabetes?

options.A: Chronic high blood pressure requiring medication
options.B: Permanent inability to digest breast milk proteins
options.C: Severe dehydration from lack of body fluids
options.D: Hypoglycemia due to ongoing high insulin production

question: How does lowering sympathetic nervous system activity help reduce blood pressure?

options.A: By increasing the total volume of circulating blood
options.B: By decreasing peripheral vascular resistance
options.C: By increasing the resting heart rate significantly
options.D: By blocking sodium retention in the renal tubules

explanation: Reducing sympathetic tone relaxes blood vessels throughout the body, lowering the resistance against which the heart pumps and thereby reducing blood pressure. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the main use of non-opioid analgesics in midwifery?

options.A: Stopping severe postpartum hemorrhage
options.B: Inducing deep general anesthesia
options.C: Speeding up active labor contractions
options.D: Relieving mild to moderate pain

question: A newborn has a congenital diaphragmatic hernia and needs breathing support. Which method should the midwife avoid if possible?

options.A: Continuous heart rate monitoring

options.D: Supplemental oxygen administration

question: Which part of the PowerPoint screen is meant for typing speaker reminders and talking points?

options.A: The notes pane

question: Which area should a midwife suction first when clearing secretions from a newborn?

options.A: The nose before the mouth
options.B: Both nostrils at the exact same time

options.D: The mouth before the nose

question: What is the maximum number of days sperm can survive inside the female reproductive tract?

options.A: Two days

question: What is considered the most reliable daily indicator of fluid retention in a hospitalized patient?

options.A: Frequency of bowel movements
options.B: Daily blood sugar checks
options.C: Abdominal girth measurement
options.D: Daily body weight measurement

explanation: Even small, rapid shifts in body weight reflect changes in fluid volume much faster than physical inspection alone. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T4#BMP216_U1_T4_h6)

question: What specialized rehydration solution is preferred over standard oral rehydration salt solution for severe malnutrition?

options.A: Normal saline
options.B: 5% Dextrose water
options.C: Fruit juice dilution
options.D: ReSoMal

explanation: ReSoMal (Rehydration Solution for Malnutrition) contains less sodium and more potassium to match the altered electrolyte balance in malnourished children. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T2#BMP118_U4_T2_h7)

question: A pregnant woman at 34 weeks comes to the clinic saying she has not felt her baby move all morning. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Reassure her that babies sleep all day inside the womb
options.B: Send her home to rest and return next week
options.C: Assess fetal heart tones and check for possible distress
options.D: Prescribe heavy iron tablets for anemia

question: Why is it important for field managers to stay flexible when unexpected issues pop up?

options.A: To ensure that interviews are rushed and completed in record time
options.B: To avoid ever having to report problems to the ethics committee
options.C: To adapt safely to changing local conditions without risking staff
options.D: To change the research hypothesis to match whatever data is easiest

explanation: Unforeseen events require quick, safe adaptations to protect the research team and maintain the study's momentum. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T4#BMP225_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is the main cause of secondary peritonitis?

options.A: Direct perforation or trauma of an intra-abdominal organ
options.B: Recurrent low-virulence fungal growth in intensive care patients
options.C: Ascites fluid becoming infected without any organ rupture
options.D: Spontaneous blood-borne spread from a distant skin infection

explanation: Secondary peritonitis happens when an internal organ ruptures or leaks its contents directly into the sterile abdominal cavity, such as a burst appendix. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T7#BMP125_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is a long-term complication caused by scar tissue inside the uterus from aggressive curettage?

options.A: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.B: Asherman's syndrome
options.C: Chronic cervical incompetence
options.D: Gestational trophoblastic disease

explanation: Asherman's syndrome involves scar tissue forming inside the uterine cavity, which can cause painful periods and secondary infertility. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h8)

question: A woman after delivery passes very little urine over a 4-hour period despite drinking well. What is the immediate midwifery priority?

options.A: Discharge her home with instructions to drink plenty of water
options.B: Reassure the relatives that the kidneys are resting after the hard work of labour
options.C: Assess vital signs, review fluid balance, and report the low urine output urgently
options.D: Wait for another six hours to see if her bladder fills up naturally

question: What is the main use of the WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria in family planning?

options.A: To calculate failure rates of barrier methods

question: Why is the postnatal period a high-risk time for women with substance use disorders?

options.A: Breastmilk neutralizes any remaining drugs in the mother's body
options.B: Postnatal clinics never allow women with a history of drug use to attend
options.C: Exhaustion and newborn demands can trigger a relapse
options.D: Hormones immediately erase all past memories of addiction

explanation: The physical and emotional stress of caring for a newborn on little sleep can overwhelm coping skills and raise relapse risk. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T8#BMP223_U3_T8_h8)

question: How do the secretions of the prostate and bulbourethral glands work together regarding acidity?

options.A: One creates acid while the other creates a base
options.B: They remove all acid from the male reproductive tract
options.C: Both secrete alkaline substances to neutralize acids
options.D: They make the semen acidic to match the vagina

explanation: Both the prostate and bulbourethral glands provide alkaline fluids that neutralize harmful acids found in the urethra and vagina. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T3#BMP210_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why should a midwife view the whole community as part of her patient group?

options.A: Because midwives are legally required to manage every household in the district

question: Why must a midwife check that there is no second twin before giving oxytocin?

options.A: Giving oxytocin early prevents the second twin from turning head-first
options.B: Oxytocin causes strong contractions that could harm an undelivered second twin
options.C: National guidelines prohibit medication until all placental tissue is out
options.D: The second twin will absorb the drug through the shared placenta

question: How should non-reassuring fetal heart patterns be handled initially during an episode of maternal DKA?

options.A: Stop all maternal insulin infusions until the baby's heart rate normalizes
options.B: Focus primarily on aggressive maternal fluid resuscitation and metabolic stabilization
options.C: Administer high-dose oxytocin to speed up vaginal delivery
options.D: Perform immediate emergency Caesarean section regardless of maternal stability

question: Which condition is a clear sign that an asphyxiated newborn needs to be transferred to a higher-level facility?

question: What is the main benefit of active immunization compared to passive immunization?

options.A: It requires no biological interaction with the immune system

options.C: It provides immediate defense within the first few hours

question: What is the safest file format to use when sharing official text documents and reports via email?

question: Which of the following describes the movement of carbon dioxide during pulmonary gas exchange?

question: What is the main goal of partner notification slips given to patients in the clinic?

question: Why should a patient finish all her antibiotics even if her symptoms go away early?

question: A pregnant woman at term experiences a natural physiological reduction in which specific pulmonary capacity?

question: What is the main role of human placental lactogen in metabolism during pregnancy?

question: Why are patients advised to take bromocriptine tablets with food or a meal?

question: How can Nigerian midwives best apply global ethical standards when working with limited medical supplies?

question: During an IUCD procedure, how long should the midwife usually leave the threads showing?

question: A student measures a baby's head by wrapping the tape under the chin and across the forehead. What should you do?

question: Through which process do waste products move from the blood into the dialysate fluid across a membrane?

question: What parts of the baby's body must form a straight line during proper feeding alignment?

question: What is a major limitation of using only the built-in spelling and grammar checker for medical documents?

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard goal of medical care for acute tonsillitis?

question: Which of these conditions would most likely cause an absent rooting reflex across both sides of the face?

question: A patient with an inevitable abortion has a pulse of 115 beats per minute, pale skin, and heavy vaginal bleeding. What should the midwife do immediately?

question: How does tubal ligation affect a woman's regular menstrual cycle and sexual response?

question: Which patient requires the highest level of direct nursing observation?

question: Which symptom combined with constipation requires immediate medical referral for a possible bowel obstruction?

question: Why is accurate blood pressure monitoring especially critical in antenatal care units?

question: What dangerous practice must midwives actively discourage when a child swallows kerosene or bleach?

question: Which test tells you the most about whether the baby is okay during early bleeding?

question: A patient presents with fever, night sweats, weight loss, and back pain with spinal deformity. Which condition is most likely present?

question: Why must hands remain elevated above the elbows after a surgical scrub?

question: Why do some newborns show withdrawal symptoms shortly after birth?

question: What type of vessel carries unfiltered lymph INTO a lymph node?

question: What is the most serious effect of severe iodine deficiency during pregnancy on the baby?

question: How should a midwife respond when community members express fear or spread rumors about a health campaign?

question: A rural health post receives a donation of complex laboratory blood analyzers that require constant air conditioning and imported chemical reagents. What makes this equipment inappropriate for the setting?

question: What common childhood problem is reduced by making sure children get enough Vitamin A?

question: Why are dietary fats extra important for children under two years old?

question: Which cell part is found in very high numbers inside heart muscle cells to supply constant energy?

options.A: Centrioles
options.B: Ribosomes
options.C: Lysosomes
options.D: Mitochondria

question: What causes the placenta to peel away from the uterine wall right after the baby is born?

options.A: The sudden rush of amniotic fluid pushing it down
options.B: The continuous pumping action of the fetal heart
options.C: The forceful pulling of the umbilical cord by the attendant

question: During a home birth, a mother's pulse rises from 80 to 110 beats per minute alongside a rising temperature. What does this suggest?

question: Why is skin-to-skin contact encouraged immediately following a home delivery?

options.D: To measure the exact birth weight of the infant

question: Which of the following is a warning sign that requires a client with dysmenorrhea to seek immediate medical review?

options.C: A slight decrease in energy levels during menses
options.D: Sudden high fever and foul-smelling vaginal discharge

question: What is the main job of the epididymis?

question: How does regular aerobic exercise help manage premenstrual syndrome symptoms?
